rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')
rules.description: Writing user input directly to an HTTP header makes code vulnerable to attack by header splitting.

rules.cwe_name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
rules.description: A Unicode transformation is using a remote user-controlled data. The transformation is a Unicode normalization using the algorithms "NFC" or "NFKC". In all cases, the security measures implemented or the logical validation performed to escape any injection characters, to validate using regex pattern

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
rules.description: user provided command can lead to execute code on a external server that can be belong to other users or admins

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Finds uses of symmetric cryptography algorithms that are weak, obsolete, or otherwise unaccepted. The key lengths allowed are 128, 192, and 256 bits. These are all the key lengths supported by AES, so any application of AES is considered acceptable.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: Use of a non-constant-time verification routine to check the value of an HTTP header, possibly allowing a timing attack to infer the header's expected value.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Less Trusted Source
rules.description: A remote endpoint identifier is read from an HTTP header. Attackers can modify the value of the identifier to forge the client ip.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
rules.description: The built-in function 'input' is used which, in Python 2, can allow arbitrary code to be run.
